title: Affordable housing incentive pilot and Rockway Centre plan
subtitle: Also covers Rosenberg-area community centre budget and name, Dumfries Avenue traffic calming, and a Greek Food Festival noise exemption.
overview: The Community and Infrastructure Services Committee recommended a new pilot program to help not-for-profit and co-op groups start affordable rental housing. It would offer $10,000 per unit, up to 50 units per project, to cover early costs before a building permit. The committee added a financial viability review to the eligibility criteria and asked staff to consider a mentorship program. The vote was unanimous on a recorded vote {{vote:m3}}.

The committee also recommended that staff proceed with a three-phase plan to replace the Rockway Centre, the city's dedicated older adult centre. The plan starts with a request for information to potential partners. Separately, it recommended a total budget for a new Rosenberg-area community centre, to be built with the Catholic school board and paid for entirely from development charges, so there is no effect on property taxes. It would be named The Williamsburg Community Centre {{vote:m5}}.

The committee recommended a traffic calming plan for Dumfries Avenue and a noise exemption for the Greek Food Festival on Bridgeport Road in June. These recommendations go to Council for a final decision.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended a new policy and a reallocation of Affordable Housing Reserve funds for the pilot, with delegated signing authority, a financial viability review and a possible mentorship program.
The committee recommended that staff proceed with the three-phase strategy to replace Rockway Centre with a new older adult centre.
The committee recommended an $8,125,000 total budget funded fully by development charges, and the name The Williamsburg Community Centre, for the centre built jointly with the Catholic school board.
The committee recommended that staff implement the proposed traffic calming plan for Dumfries Avenue.
The committee recommended a Chapter 450 noise exemption for the festival at 527 Bridgeport Road on June 8 and 9.

debate: Delegates from housing providers said upfront costs such as design and approvals are a major barrier for not-for-profits, which often lack development expertise. They supported staged funding with accountability checkpoints and a mentorship program.

Some councillors asked whether eligibility would exclude groups new to development, such as a church planning housing on its land. Staff said applicants need a not-for-profit housing developer with past build experience, which can come through a partnership. They said a co-op in good standing could apply.

One councillor asked that priority for deeply affordable and supportive units be changed from "may" to "will". Staff said not every project can be fully deeply affordable, so the wording stays flexible.

On Rockway Centre, councillors asked about disruption to programs, the timeline and whether the request for information would narrow the field of bidders. Staff called the second-quarter 2025 timeline aggressive and said the request is non-binding and does not exclude later bidders.

On the Rosenberg-area centre, staff said the joint build with the school board saves money compared with a standalone facility. Councillors pressed for a firm opening date, which staff said depends on the school board.
